41/G.goal: Explain how the Majuli VR tour's system design translated its development-lifecycle objectives, user categories, and information points into an immersive entry experience, media and interface design, and comfort-aware navigation.
41/G.achieves: This gives the learner a concrete case-study model of the system design stage, so they can design an XR system with coherent content, interaction, orientation, and comfort decisions before implementation.

41/O1.goal: Explain how the Majuli VR tour's design was framed by the interactive system development lifecycle, its objectives, user categories, and 24 information points.
41/O1.achieves: This lets the learner identify how user categories and information points constrain the content scope of an XR system before detailed design begins.

41/O2.goal: Describe how the Majuli VR tour's starting experience, visual and video media, and ambient sounds were designed to establish an immersive context.
41/O2.achieves: This prepares the learner to plan onboarding, media preprocessing, and sound design choices that support presence and quality of experience in XR.

41/O3.goal: Describe how the virtual tablet, minimaps, arrows, and notifications were designed to provide navigation tools, information access, and wayfinding support.
41/O3.achieves: This gives the learner a pattern for designing interface and orientation tools that help users locate themselves and discover content in an XR environment.

41/O4.goal: Explain how vehicle-based travel, smooth transitions, location-relevant content cues, and controlled navigation were used to support exploration while minimizing cybersickness.
41/O4.achieves: This enables the learner to choose locomotion, transition, and visual control techniques that balance explorability, content discovery, and user comfort in an XR system.
